# TJ Live — TransJakarta Real-Time Bus Tracker\
\
Permalink: TJ Live — TransJakarta Real-Time Bus Tracker\
\
Real-time visualization of ~2,800 TransJakarta buses on a dark-themed map. Built with SvelteKit, MapLibre GL, and MQTT WebSocket streaming.\
\
## Features\
\
Permalink: Features\
\
- 🗺️ **Live Map** — Real-time bus positions on CartoDB Dark Matter basemap\
- 🚌 **2,800+ Buses** — All TransJakarta bus types (BRT, Mikrotrans, Royaltrans, etc.)\
- ⚡ **MQTT Streaming** — WebSocket connection to `wss://mqtt.tj.co.id:8084/mqtt` for instant updates\
- 🔄 **REST Fallback** — Automatic failover to polling when MQTT is unavailable\
- 📍 **Nearby Stops** — Geolocation-based stop discovery\
- 🗓️ **Route Browser** — Paginated route list with search and detail views\
- 🧭 **Trip Planning** — A→B directions with transit route options\
- 🔍 **Place Search** — Google Places autocomplete via TransJakarta API proxy\
- 📱 **PWA Ready** — Standalone mode, dark theme, installable\
- ♿ **Accessible** — ARIA landmarks, keyboard navigation, screen reader support\
\
## Tech Stack\
\
Permalink: Tech Stack\
\
| Layer | Technology |\
| --- | --- |\
| Framework | SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 (runes) |\
| Language | TypeScript |\
| Styling | Tailwind CSS v4 + CSS Custom Properties |\
| Map | MapLibre GL JS + svelte-maplibre-gl |\

| Auth | jose (JWT decode) |\
| Deploy | Cloudflare Pages (adapter-cloudflare) |\
| Analytics | Google Analytics 4 (gtag.js) |\

## Project Structure\
\
Permalink: Project Structure\
\
```\
src/\
├── routes/\
│   ├── +layout.svelte          # App shell (header, nav, toast)\
│   ├── +page.svelte            # Home (map + live buses)\
│   ├── routes/                 # Route browser\
│   │   ├── +page.svelte        # Route list (SSR)\
│   │   └── [id]/+page.svelte   # Route detail (SSR)\
│   ├── stops/                  # Stop browser\
│   │   ├── +page.svelte        # Nearby stops (geolocation)\
│   │   └── [id]/+page.svelte   # Stop detail\
│   ├── directions/+page.svelte # Trip planning\
│   └── api/                    # Server-side API proxies (9 routes)\
├── lib/\
│   ├── components/             # Svelte components\
│   ├── stores/                 # State management (MQTT, REST, toast)\
│   ├── server/                 # Server-only code (JWT manager)\
│   ├── types/                  # TypeScript type definitions\
│   └── styles/                 # Design tokens\
└── app.html                    # HTML shell with PWA meta tags\
```\
\
## API Architecture\
\
Permalink: API Architecture\
\
The app proxies all TransJakarta API calls through SvelteKit server routes to:\
\
- Handle JWT authentication (guest login, token caching, auto-refresh)\
- Inject required headers (X-Device-ID, X-App-Version, User-Agent)\
- Hide API implementation details from the client\
\
## Analytics\
\
Permalink: Analytics\
\
The app uses Google Analytics 4 (GA4) for basic usage tracking.\
\
### Setup\
\
Permalink: Setup\
\
1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env`\
2. Set `PUBLIC_GA4_ID` to your GA4 Measurement ID (e.g., `G-TTN4XHEDY2`)\
\
### How It Works\
\
Permalink: How It Works\
\
- **Page views** — Automatically tracked on every SPA navigation via `Analytics.svelte`\
- **Home events** — User interactions on the home panel (geolocation, mode changes, etc.) via `trackHomeEvent()` in `src/lib/telemetry/home.ts`\
- **Detail views** — Route and stop detail page views\
- **Direction searches** — Trip planning queries\
\
### Privacy\
\
Permalink: Privacy\
\
- GA4 anonymizes IP addresses by default\
- No personal data is collected\
- Ad blockers can safely block GA4 — all tracking is no-op resilient\
\
## Deployment\
\
Permalink: Deployment\
\
Configured for Cloudflare Pages with:\
\
- `adapter-cloudflare` with `nodejs_compat` \+ `nodejs_als` flags\
- Jakarta (CGK) data center for low-latency access from Indonesia\
- Zero cold starts via Cloudflare Workers runtime\

Transjakarta and Google present real-time information on Transjakarta buses on Google Maps. This new information allows users to track their bus location in real time, making it easier to plan trips and avoid delays.

Starting today, users can access real-time Transjakarta bus data directly via Google Maps on smartphones and other devices. If a Transjakarta route is available, real-time information will be displayed clearly in the search results. This integration allows passengers to make informed travel decisions, plan trips more effectively, and reduce waiting times, contributing to a more efficient and reliable public transportation experience in Jakarta.

- Open Google Maps : Make sure you have the latest version of the Google Maps app installed on your device.

# Transjakarta (Official PT Transportasi Jakarta GTFS)

Transjakarta bus routes with the halte they serve, fares, and departure headways.

Sign Up Free View Full Docs

Data as of 26 Sept 2026 · Source: Official Transjakarta GTFS

Main endpointGET https://use.apiindonesia.id/api/v1/transjakarta/ruteEndpoints7Authenticationx-api-key header (create one free in the dashboard)Price2 credits (Rp2) per successful request; failed requests are freeFormatJSON (REST), with cURL, JavaScript and Python examplesData sourceSource: GTFS Static Transjakarta (c) 2026 by PT Transportasi Jakarta, licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0); Licence statement: https://ppid.transjakarta.co.id/informasi/berkala; Source file: https://gtfs.transjakarta.co.id/files/file\_gtfs.zip; Attribution: the licence requires attribution, a licence link, and an indication of changes. Every successful response carries meta.attribution with the publisher, the licence name, a licence link, a link to the source file, the licence-statement page, and the statement of changes "Data diubah: dinormalisasi ke format JSON API Indonesia", so you do not have to assemble the credit yourself, just pass that object through in every redistribution; What API Indonesia changed: the GTFS was normalised to JSON, the stop\_times rows were condensed into one stop list per route and direction, and shapes.txt (geometry) is not included in this version

Product Brief

## What this API gives you

Transjakarta bus routes with the halte they serve, fares, and departure headways.

- Bus routes with the halte they serve
- Nearest-halte search from a coordinate
- Fares
- Per-route departure headways
- Data: the official static GTFS published by PT Transportasi Jakarta, licensed CC BY 4.0, reusable commercially as long as the attribution is kept

- Source: GTFS Static Transjakarta (c) 2026 by PT Transportasi Jakarta, licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0)
- Licence statement: https://ppid.transjakarta.co.id/informasi/berkala
- Source file: https://gtfs.transjakarta.co.id/files/file\_gtfs.zip
- Attribution: the licence requires attribution, a licence link, and an indication of changes. Every successful response carries meta.attribution with the publisher, the licence name, a licence link, a link to the source file, the licence-statement page, and the statement of changes "Data diubah: dinormalisasi ke format JSON API Indonesia", so you do not have to assemble the credit yourself, just pass that object through in every redistribution
- What API Indonesia changed: the GTFS was normalised to JSON, the stop\_times rows were condensed into one stop list per route and direction, and shapes.txt (geometry) is not included in this version

Coverage

7

ready-to-use endpoints in this product, with JSON responses and consistent error handling.

Access

API key

Can be tried with the 3,000 credit signup bonus, then used in production through one API Indonesia key.

Sample resource

`https://use.apiindonesia.id/api/v1/transjakarta/rute`

Returns the 240 Transjakarta routes.

### Example product scenarios

This section separates the product page from the docs. The docs explain how to call endpoints; this page explains why the endpoints make sense for your feature.

- Mobility & map apps: display Transjakarta routes and halte, find the nearest halte to a user, and build arrival estimates from the official headways.
- Transport research & urban planning: analyse halte coverage per route, headway patterns, and the fare structure without importing the large GTFS files yourself.
- Logistics & field apps: compute the nearest halte or route from a customer point, and use the halte list for location search and address validation.

## Example Usage

curl "https://use.apiindonesia.id/api/v1/transjakarta/rute?q=blok&per_page=2" \

## Transjakarta (Official PT Transportasi Jakarta GTFS) API questions

### Which Transjakarta data is available?

Routes with the halte they serve, nearest-halte search from a coordinate, fares and per-route departure headways, from the official static GTFS by PT Transportasi Jakarta.

### How do I find the nearest halte?

Call GET /api/v1/transjakarta/halte/nearby with lat, lng and optional radius and limit.

tool_result.tool_observation:
This is the vanilla extracted tool response: Transitous uses data from public sources in the GTFS file format.

We process the data to make sure it is syntactically and (mostly) semantically correct, and make the resulting GTFS files available for use again.

If necessary, we remove parts of the data from a source if it overlaps with a better source.
Therefore the processed version does not necessarily cover the same area as the original. Only use it in combination with the other files for the region.

Data from OpenStreetMap is used directly and indirectly for street routing, geocoding, map tiles and stops and lines metadata.

Elevation data from Mapterhorn and its sources is used for the hillshades in the web UI. Elevation data from SRTM is used for the incline calculation in street routing.

content_list.content:
# Yes — but there's no *official public* developer API. Here's what actually works (verified today)

## TL;DR

Transjakarta does **not** offer an official, documented public API program (no developer portal, no API key signup). However, real-time bus tracking data **is accessible** through the backend of their official "TJ: Transjakarta" app, and community projects have reverse-engineered it successfully. I tested the endpoints live today (Nov 19, 2026) and they work. There's also an officially open **static GTFS** feed.

---

## Option 1: The TJ App Backend (unofficial, but working) ✅

This is the stack powering the official TJ:Transjakarta app, documented by community projects like [tj-live](https://github.com/mugnimaestra/tj-live) [[2]] and [open-tj](https://github.com/BroNils/open-tj) [[39]], and independently verified in [this research writeup](https://git.rasyidanaf.com/0xrsydn/research/src/branch/main/transjakarta-live-data/sources.md) [[41]].

### A. REST API — `https://tijeapi.transjakarta.co.id`

**I verified this end-to-end just now.** Guest login works without any registration:

```python
import requests

BASE = "https://tijeapi.transjakarta.co.id"
headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "User-Agent": "okhttp/4.12.0",
    "X-App-OS": "android",
    "X-App-Version": "2.10.2",
    "X-Device-ID": "your-unique-device-id",
}

# 1. Get a guest JWT (no account needed)
r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/v1/auth/login/guest",
                  json={"device_id": "your-unique-device-id"}, headers=headers)
token = r.json()["token"]  # or ["data"]["token"]
headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"

# 2. Get live bus positions near a coordinate (radius in km)
r = requests.get(f"{BASE}/v1/bus",
                 params={"latitude": -6.1754, "longitude": 106.8272, "radius": 1},
                 headers=headers)
buses = r.json()["data"]
```

My test returned **39 live buses** near Monas with fields including: `bus_body_no`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `speed`, `bearing`, `route_code`, `route_name`, `type` (BRT/Mikrotrans/etc.), `next_stops`, `estimated_time_next_stops`, `trip_id`, `trip_headsign`, and `timestamp`. The GPS timestamps were **~10 seconds old** — genuinely real-time. Sample record:

```json
{
  "bus_body_no": "SAF-053",
  "latitude": -6.17617, "longitude": 106.823042,
  "speed": 0, "bearing": 185,
  "route_code": "2", "route_name": "Pulo Gadung", "type": "BRT",
  "next_stops": "H00006P-Balai Kota"
}
```

⚠️ Note: a radius of 50 km returns ~29 MB (each bus carries a full `stops` array — strip it), and large requests can time out. Use small radii or strip heavy fields like tj-live does.

### B. MQTT streaming — `wss://mqtt.tj.co.id:8084/mqtt`

For true push-based tracking (~2,800 buses), the app uses **MQTT 3.1.1 over WebSocket with anonymous access** [[41]]:

1. `POST /v1/bus` with `{"latitude": ..., "longitude": ..., "radius": ..., "event": "change_loc"}` → returns a list of MQTT **topics** (I got 1,824 topics like `/mobile_armada/0014-0018/#`)
2. Connect to the broker and subscribe to those topics → JSON position updates stream in per bus [[2]]

**Caveat from my testing:** the REST API (`tijeapi`, port 443) was reachable from my sandbox, but `mqtt.tj.co.id:8084` timed out — while other public MQTT brokers on similar ports worked fine. This suggests the broker may be **geo-restricted (Indonesia-only) or firewalled**. If you're in Indonesia it will likely work (tj-live demonstrably uses it); from overseas servers, plan on the REST polling fallback (e.g., poll every 10 s).

## Option 2: Official static GTFS (open, CC BY 4.0) ✅

- **Direct download (verified working, HTTP 200, ~2.5 MB):** `https://gtfs.transjakarta.co.id/files/file_gtfs.zip` — routes, stops, schedules, shapes; updated roughly weekly [[41]]
- Licensed **CC BY 4.0** — free for commercial use with attribution [[26]]
- Also mirrored on [Transitland](https://www.transit.land/data/feeds/f-transjakarta~id) (84 archived versions) [[48]]
- **No public GTFS-Realtime feed exists**: Transitland's registry lists only the static feed for Transjakarta [[107]]. TJ built GTFS-RT internally to power Google Maps live tracking [[15]], but that feed goes to Google, not the public [[1]].

## Option 3: Third-party wrappers

- **[apiindonesia.id](https://apiindonesia.id/en/produk/transjakarta/)** — paid REST wrapper (Rp2/request), but **static GTFS only**, no live positions [[26]]
- **[open-tj](https://github.com/BroNils/open-tj)** — unofficial Go SDK wrapping ~105 REST endpoints + MQTT tracking [[39]]
- **[tj-live](https://github.com/mugnimaestra/tj-live)** — full SvelteKit reference implementation (JWT handling, MQTT, REST fallback) you can study [[21]]
- The old `api.hackjak.bappedajakarta.go.id` Busway API [[17]] is long dead — don't bother.

---

## Important caveats

1. **Unofficial ≠ guaranteed.** The `tijeapi`/MQTT endpoints are the app's private backend. No SLA, no terms permitting third-party use, and they can change or lock down anytime (the app mimics Android headers for a reason). Fine for personal projects/research; risky for production.
2. **For legitimate/commercial access**, contact PT Transportasi Jakarta directly (or via Jakarta's open-data channel `data.jakarta.go.id` [[56]]) to request formal data-sharing — especially for the GTFS-RT feed they already produce for Google.
3. **Practical recipe:** static GTFS (official, stable) for routes/stops + `GET /v1/bus` polling (works globally, verified) for live positions + MQTT if your server can reach the broker.

Want me to sketch a complete minimal tracker script (guest auth + token refresh + polling loop), or dig into the MQTT topic/message schema?

# TJ Live — TransJakarta Real-Time Bus Tracker\
\
Permalink: TJ Live — TransJakarta Real-Time Bus Tracker\
\
Real-time visualization of ~2,800 TransJakarta buses on a dark-themed map. Built with SvelteKit, MapLibre GL, and MQTT WebSocket streaming.\
\
## Features\
\
Permalink: Features\
\
- 🗺️ **Live Map** — Real-time bus positions on CartoDB Dark Matter basemap\
- 🚌 **2,800+ Buses** — All TransJakarta bus types (BRT, Mikrotrans, Royaltrans, etc.)\
- ⚡ **MQTT Streaming** — WebSocket connection to `wss://mqtt.tj.co.id:8084/mqtt` for instant updates\
- 🔄 **REST Fallback** — Automatic failover to polling when MQTT is unavailable\
- 📍 **Nearby Stops** — Geolocation-based stop discovery\
- 🗓️ **Route Browser** — Paginated route list with search and detail views\
- 🧭 **Trip Planning** — A→B directions with transit route options\
- 🔍 **Place Search** — Google Places autocomplete via TransJakarta API proxy\
- 📱 **PWA Ready** — Standalone mode, dark theme, installable\
- ♿ **Accessible** — ARIA landmarks, keyboard navigation, screen reader support\
\
## Tech Stack\
\
Permalink: Tech Stack\
\
| Layer | Technology |\
| --- | --- |\
| Framework | SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 (runes) |\
| Language | TypeScript |\
| Styling | Tailwind CSS v4 + CSS Custom Properties |\
| Map | MapLibre GL JS + svelte-maplibre-gl |\
| Real-time | MQTT.js (WSS) + REST polling fallback |\
| Auth | jose (JWT decode) |\
| Deploy | Cloudflare Pages (adapter-cloudflare) |\
| Analytics | Google Analytics 4 (gtag.js) |\
| Basemap | CartoDB Dark Matter (free, no API key) |\
\
## Getting Started\
\
Permalink: Getting Started\
\
### Prerequisites\
\
Permalink: Prerequisites\
\
- Node.js 20+\
- npm 10+\
\
### Development\
\
Permalink: Development\
\
```\
cd transjakarta-re/webapp\
npm install\
npm run dev\
```\
\
### Build\
\
Permalink: Build\
\
```\
npm run build\
npm run preview   # local preview\
```\
\
### Type Check\
\
Permalink: Type Check\
\
```\
npm run check\
```\
\
## Project Structure\
\
Permalink: Project Structure\
\
```\
src/\
├── routes/\
│   ├── +layout.svelte          # App shell (header, nav, toast)\
│   ├── +page.svelte            # Home (map + live buses)\
│   ├── routes/                 # Route browser\
│   │   ├── +page.svelte        # Route list (SSR)\
│   │   └── [id]/+page.svelte   # Route detail (SSR)\
│   ├── stops/                  # Stop browser\
│   │   ├── +page.svelte        # Nearby stops (geolocation)\
│   │   └── [id]/+page.svelte   # Stop detail\
│   ├── directions/+page.svelte # Trip planning\
│   └── api/                    # Server-side API proxies (9 routes)\
├── lib/\
│   ├── components/             # Svelte components\
│   ├── stores/                 # State management (MQTT, REST, toast)\
│   ├── server/                 # Server-only code (JWT manager)\
│   ├── types/                  # TypeScript type definitions\
│   └── styles/                 # Design tokens\
└── app.html                    # HTML shell with PWA meta tags\
```\
\
## API Architecture\
\
Permalink: API Architecture\
\
The app proxies all TransJakarta API calls through SvelteKit server routes to:\
\
- Handle JWT authentication (guest login, token caching, auto-refresh)\
- Inject required headers (X-Device-ID, X-App-Version, User-Agent)\
- Hide API implementation details from the client\
\
## Analytics\
\
Permalink: Analytics\
\
The app uses Google Analytics 4 (GA4) for basic usage tracking.\
\
### Setup\
\
Permalink: Setup\
\
1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env`\
2. Set `PUBLIC_GA4_ID` to your GA4 Measurement ID (e.g., `G-TTN4XHEDY2`)\
\
### How It Works\
\
Permalink: How It Works\
\
- **Page views** — Automatically tracked on every SPA navigation via `Analytics.svelte`\
- **Home events** — User interactions on the home panel (geolocation, mode changes, etc.) via `trackHomeEvent()` in `src/lib/telemetry/home.ts`\
- **Detail views** — Route and stop detail page views\
- **Direction searches** — Trip planning queries\
\
### Privacy\
\
Permalink: Privacy\
\
- GA4 anonymizes IP addresses by default\
- No personal data is collected\
- Ad blockers can safely block GA4 — all tracking is no-op resilient\
\
## Deployment\
\
Permalink: Deployment\
\
Configured for Cloudflare Pages with:\
\
- `adapter-cloudflare` with `nodejs_compat` \+ `nodejs_als` flags\
- Jakarta (CGK) data center for low-latency access from Indonesia\
- Zero cold starts via Cloudflare Workers runtime\
\

Real-Time Transjakarta Information Now Available on Google Maps

Transjakarta and Google present real-time information on Transjakarta buses on Google Maps. This new information allows users to track their bus location in real time, making it easier to plan trips and avoid delays.

Starting today, users can access real-time Transjakarta bus data directly via Google Maps on smartphones and other devices. If a Transjakarta route is available, real-time information will be displayed clearly in the search results. This integration allows passengers to make informed travel decisions, plan trips more effectively, and reduce waiting times, contributing to a more efficient and reliable public transportation experience in Jakarta.

"We are very pleased to collaborate with Google on this initiative. The availability of real-time information for Transjakarta buses on Google Maps marks a significant step in improving the quality of our service and providing a better commuting experience for Transjakarta customers. This information is expected to significantly reduce waiting times and improving travel planning, so that the daily experience of using public transportation can be more comfortable for all residents of Jakarta and its surroundings.

In the last few months, we and Google have continued to strive to display more accurate data, ensuring that the features and technology we collaborate on can be used by Transjakarta customers well. We appreciate Google's dedication to continuing to collaborate with Transjakarta, supporting Jakarta's public transportation system, and their commitment to utilizing technology to improve the quality of life for Jakarta residents. This partnership shows how technology can be utilized for a smarter city, this is also in line with how Jakarta is building its vision as Jakarta a Global City." - Main Director of Transjakarta, Welfizon Yuza

**How to Use the Real-Time Feature in Google Maps**

- Open Google Maps : Make sure you have the latest version of the Google Maps app installed on your device.
- Find Your Route : Enter your destination and select public transportation options.
- Select Transjakarta : Select Transjakarta as the mode of transportation you want.
- View Real-Time Information : Check real-time bus locations, estimated arrival times, and service alerts or disruptions on your route.
- Set Alerts : Choose to receive notifications about changes or delays on your selected route.

- Logistics & field apps: compute the nearest halte or route from a customer point, and use the halte list for location search and address validation.

tool_result.tool_observation:
This is the vanilla extracted tool response: Transitous uses data from public sources in the GTFS file format.

We process the data to make sure it is syntactically and (mostly) semantically correct, and make the resulting GTFS files available for use again.

If necessary, we remove parts of the data from a source if it overlaps with a better source.
Therefore the processed version does not necessarily cover the same area as the original. Only use it in combination with the other files for the region.

Data from OpenStreetMap is used directly and indirectly for street routing, geocoding, map tiles and stops and lines metadata.

Elevation data from Mapterhorn and its sources is used for the hillshades in the web UI. Elevation data from SRTM is used for the incline calculation in street routing.

# Yes — but there's no *official public* developer API. Here's what actually works (verified today)

## TL;DR

Transjakarta does **not** offer an official, documented public API program (no developer portal, no API key signup). However, real-time bus tracking data **is accessible** through the backend of their official "TJ: Transjakarta" app, and community projects have reverse-engineered it successfully. I tested the endpoints live today (Nov 19, 2026) and they work. There's also an officially open **static GTFS** feed.

---

## Option 1: The TJ App Backend (unofficial, but working) ✅

This is the stack powering the official TJ:Transjakarta app, documented by community projects like [tj-live](https://github.com/mugnimaestra/tj-live) [[2]] and [open-tj](https://github.com/BroNils/open-tj) [[39]], and independently verified in [this research writeup](https://git.rasyidanaf.com/0xrsydn/research/src/branch/main/transjakarta-live-data/sources.md) [[41]].

### A. REST API — `https://tijeapi.transjakarta.co.id`

**I verified this end-to-end just now.** Guest login works without any registration:

```python
import requests

BASE = "https://tijeapi.transjakarta.co.id"
headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "User-Agent": "okhttp/4.12.0",
    "X-App-OS": "android",
    "X-App-Version": "2.10.2",
    "X-Device-ID": "your-unique-device-id",
}

# 1. Get a guest JWT (no account needed)
r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/v1/auth/login/guest",
                  json={"device_id": "your-unique-device-id"}, headers=headers)
token = r.json()["token"]  # or ["data"]["token"]
headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"

# 2. Get live bus positions near a coordinate (radius in km)
r = requests.get(f"{BASE}/v1/bus",
                 params={"latitude": -6.1754, "longitude": 106.8272, "radius": 1},
                 headers=headers)
buses = r.json()["data"]
```

My test returned **39 live buses** near Monas with fields including: `bus_body_no`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `speed`, `bearing`, `route_code`, `route_name`, `type` (BRT/Mikrotrans/etc.), `next_stops`, `estimated_time_next_stops`, `trip_id`, `trip_headsign`, and `timestamp`. The GPS timestamps were **~10 seconds old** — genuinely real-time. Sample record:

```json
{
  "bus_body_no": "SAF-053",
  "latitude": -6.17617, "longitude": 106.823042,
  "speed": 0, "bearing": 185,
  "route_code": "2", "route_name": "Pulo Gadung", "type": "BRT",
  "next_stops": "H00006P-Balai Kota"
}
```

⚠️ Note: a radius of 50 km returns ~29 MB (each bus carries a full `stops` array — strip it), and large requests can time out. Use small radii or strip heavy fields like tj-live does.

### B. MQTT streaming — `wss://mqtt.tj.co.id:8084/mqtt`

For true push-based tracking (~2,800 buses), the app uses **MQTT 3.1.1 over WebSocket with anonymous access** [[41]]:

1. `POST /v1/bus` with `{"latitude": ..., "longitude": ..., "radius": ..., "event": "change_loc"}` → returns a list of MQTT **topics** (I got 1,824 topics like `/mobile_armada/0014-0018/#`)
2. Connect to the broker and subscribe to those topics → JSON position updates stream in per bus [[2]]

**Caveat from my testing:** the REST API (`tijeapi`, port 443) was reachable from my sandbox, but `mqtt.tj.co.id:8084` timed out — while other public MQTT brokers on similar ports worked fine. This suggests the broker may be **geo-restricted (Indonesia-only) or firewalled**. If you're in Indonesia it will likely work (tj-live demonstrably uses it); from overseas servers, plan on the REST polling fallback (e.g., poll every 10 s).

## Option 2: Official static GTFS (open, CC BY 4.0) ✅

- **Direct download (verified working, HTTP 200, ~2.5 MB):** `https://gtfs.transjakarta.co.id/files/file_gtfs.zip` — routes, stops, schedules, shapes; updated roughly weekly [[41]]
- Licensed **CC BY 4.0** — free for commercial use with attribution [[26]]
- Also mirrored on [Transitland](https://www.transit.land/data/feeds/f-transjakarta~id) (84 archived versions) [[48]]
- **No public GTFS-Realtime feed exists**: Transitland's registry lists only the static feed for Transjakarta [[107]]. TJ built GTFS-RT internally to power Google Maps live tracking [[15]], but that feed goes to Google, not the public [[1]].

## Option 3: Third-party wrappers

- **[apiindonesia.id](https://apiindonesia.id/en/produk/transjakarta/)** — paid REST wrapper (Rp2/request), but **static GTFS only**, no live positions [[26]]
- **[open-tj](https://github.com/BroNils/open-tj)** — unofficial Go SDK wrapping ~105 REST endpoints + MQTT tracking [[39]]
- **[tj-live](https://github.com/mugnimaestra/tj-live)** — full SvelteKit reference implementation (JWT handling, MQTT, REST fallback) you can study [[21]]
- The old `api.hackjak.bappedajakarta.go.id` Busway API [[17]] is long dead — don't bother.

---

## Important caveats

1. **Unofficial ≠ guaranteed.** The `tijeapi`/MQTT endpoints are the app's private backend. No SLA, no terms permitting third-party use, and they can change or lock down anytime (the app mimics Android headers for a reason). Fine for personal projects/research; risky for production.
2. **For legitimate/commercial access**, contact PT Transportasi Jakarta directly (or via Jakarta's open-data channel `data.jakarta.go.id` [[56]]) to request formal data-sharing — especially for the GTFS-RT feed they already produce for Google.
3. **Practical recipe:** static GTFS (official, stable) for routes/stops + `GET /v1/bus` polling (works globally, verified) for live positions + MQTT if your server can reach the broker.

Want me to sketch a complete minimal tracker script (guest auth + token refresh + polling loop), or dig into the MQTT topic/message schema?
